title: Earliest Shared Free Window
statement:
Two people want to book a call that lasts duration minutes. Each person gives a list of free slots, [start, end], in no particular order. One person's slots never overlap each other.

Return the earliest window [t, t + duration] that lies inside a free slot of both people. If no such window exists, return an empty array.

A slot [a, b] contains the window when a ≤ t and t + duration ≤ b.

examples.why: The first common stretch is 30 to 40, exactly 10 minutes long. A window that fills an overlap exactly still counts.
The lists are not sorted. The first slots listed overlap at 60 to 80, but 5 to 12 comes earlier in time.
The slots only touch at minute 5. A shared stretch of length 0 cannot hold any call.

constraints: Slots of the same person do not overlap
hints: Comparing every slot of one person with every slot of the other works, but it is quadratic. What order would let you walk both lists once?
Sort both lists by start time. The overlap of [a1, b1] and [a2, b2] is [max(a1, a2), min(b1, b2)]; it fits the call when its length is at least duration.
Two pointers: check the overlap of the current pair, then advance whichever slot ends first. That slot cannot overlap anything later in the other list.

explain.intuition:
Two slots share the stretch from the later start to the earlier end: [max(a1, a2), min(b1, b2)]. If that stretch is at least duration long, the call fits, and the earliest window in it starts at max(a1, a2).

To find the earliest one quickly, sort both lists by start and walk them together, like merging two sorted arrays. After checking a pair, drop the slot that ends first: every remaining slot of the other person starts later than the current one, so the dropped slot could only overlap them less. Because one person's slots do not overlap, the overlaps you meet come in time order, and the first one long enough is the answer. It is the same pattern as finding when two busy calendars are both free.
steps: While both pointers are in range: let lo = max(startA, startB) and hi = min(endA, endB).
If hi − lo ≥ duration, return [lo, lo + duration].
Otherwise advance the pointer whose slot ends earlier.
If either list runs out, return [].
pitfalls: Walking the lists in the given order. They are unsorted, as in the second example.
Returning the whole overlap instead of a window of exactly duration.
Advancing the slot that started first instead of the one that ended first. A long early slot can still overlap later slots of the other person.

complexity.time: O(n log n + m log m)
complexity.space: O(n + m) for the sorted copies

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: For every slot of A against every slot of B, compute the overlap; keep the earliest start among overlaps that are long enough.

solutions.title: Sort and walk with two pointers
solutions.idea: Sort both lists, check the overlap of the current pair, then drop whichever slot ends first.
solutions.time: O(n log n + m log m)
